title: Continuous Integration
subtopics: Failing builds when required checks fail
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of Continuous Integration and define its core vocabulary.
Apply continuous integration in a small PowerShell example and predict its result.
Identify one relevant edge case, version constraint, or troubleshooting step.

content.intro: This lesson covers Continuous Integration in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Version control, CI and release automation make changes reviewable and repeatable. Run tests and static analysis before packaging, pin or constrain dependencies, protect credentials in automation, and require approval or rollback planning for production deployment.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Continuous Integration belongs to Git, CI/CD, Deployment, and Collaboration. Focus on the rule or workflow this lesson introduces, work through a small example, and explain the expected result and one boundary case.

content_blocks.title: Build understanding step by step
content_blocks.text: Start with the syllabus concepts: Running tests automatically; Running PSScriptAnalyzer; Generating test reports; Failing builds when required checks fail. Separate the input, the operation and the expected result. Use a disposable local workspace for file or system examples, and verify platform-specific behavior against the active runtime.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Review this snippet as a static teaching example. In a local PowerShell 7.6 session, save a copy under your course workspace, run it manually, and compare the result with the stated expectation. CodeLeaf’s current course preview does not execute PowerShell. Adjust environment-dependent output to your machine.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Check command availability with Get-Command, inspect values with Get-Member, consult Get-Help -Full, and verify PowerShell version/platform before assuming identical output. Do not run examples that change system state without adapting and reviewing them.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and use synthetic values. If you created test files, delete only those files within the dedicated practice folder after checking their paths.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.

content.task: Try it yourself: apply the concept to a small reproducible automation task. Use synthetic data or a disposable practice folder, write down your predicted result, check it locally, and explain one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central idea in Continuous Integration in your own words.
Verify the expected result using a local session or a documented manual check.
Describe one relevant edge case, limitation or troubleshooting step.
hints: Predict the output before changing the example.
Change one input or condition at a time and compare the results.
Use Get-Help and official versioned documentation when behavior differs; do not treat a static preview as execution.
